source.title: PSG wide free kick: blocking the last defender in the line

situation.pitch_area: far-post zone, edge of penalty area (defensive line ~13m out)
situation.outcome: Pacho's screening block on the last defender (Falcon) frees Neves to arrive unmarked at the far post and head at goal from an inswinging delivery
situation.human_observation: This example comes from the FIFA Club World Cup 2025 game between PSG and Inter Miami. Inter Miami's defensive setup exposed the last defender in their zonal line: five players were committed to the ball/wall area, leaving only five in the zonal line itself, which created a 4v2 numerical disadvantage at the far post. The line held close to the edge of the box (~13m out), leaving space in behind. Defenders in the line adopted closed body orientations, limiting visual contact with both ball and attackers behind them, and the last defender was undersized relative to the block he'd face. The line also stepped up early, timed to the taker's run-up, which reduced attackers' ability to gain a positional edge but also let offside-starting attackers regain onside position as the kick was delivered. PSG designed their routine around these specific vulnerabilities: two attackers made runs from depth while two more held offside positions to occupy the last defenders and disguise the real threat. All movement was triggered off Vitinha's first step. Marquinhos' run pulled Falcon (the last defender) infield, further weakening far-post cover, while Neves timed his run to stay onside. Pacho, reacting to the same trigger, regained an onside position as the line stepped up early, then applied the block. PSG deliberately used Pacho — their more physically dominant centre-back — against Inter Miami's smaller last defender, and Pacho screened with his back to the defender (avoiding arm use or frontal contact) to block the recovery run without conceding a foul, while staying available for any second ball. The inswinging delivery met Neves' well-timed run from deep at the far post, arriving unmarked for a free header, while Falcon — anticipating the ball would go out of play and unaware of the run behind him due to his closed body orientation — raised his arms rather than defending the space.
situation.priority_problem: How to exploit a zonal defensive line's structural weaknesses (numerical inferiority at the far post, closed body orientation, an undersized last defender, and early/predictable line movement) by combining decoy/offside-holding runners with a timed physical screen (block) on the last defender, freeing a runner from depth to attack the far post unmarked.
visible_evidence: Inter Miami commit five players to the ball/wall area, leaving only five players in the zonal defensive line and a 4v2 numerical disadvantage at the far post.
Inter Miami's line holds roughly 13 metres from goal, close to the edge of the box, leaving space in behind.
Defenders in the line use predominantly closed body orientation, limiting awareness of attackers behind them, particularly the last defender who has no cover behind him.
Inter Miami position a smaller/less physical defender at the end of the zonal line.
The defensive line steps up early, timed to the taker's run-up, which can play onside-holding attackers back onside as the kick is delivered.
PSG position two attackers to run from depth and two more to hold offside positions, occupying/confusing the last line of defenders.
All attacking movement is synchronised off Vitinha's first step in his run-up.
Marquinhos' run drags Falcon (the last Inter Miami defender) infield, reducing far-post cover further.
Neves times his run from depth to remain onside while targeting the far post.
Pacho, triggered by the same cue, regains an onside position as the line steps up early, then executes the block.
PSG deliberately match Pacho (physically dominant) against Inter Miami's smaller last defender.

Pacho screens with his back to the defender rather than making frontal contact, avoiding arm use, blocking the defender's recovery run without conceding a foul while staying available for a second ball.
The inswinging delivery meets Neves' run at the far post, where he arrives completely unmarked for a free header on goal.
Falcon raises his arms expecting the ball to go out of play, unaware of Neves' run behind him due to his closed body orientation.

coaching.objective: Exploit a zonal defensive line's structural weaknesses at the far post — numerical inferiority, closed body orientation, an undersized last defender, and predictable early line movement — by synchronising decoy/offside-holding runners with a timed, legal screening block on the last defender to free a runner from depth for an unmarked header at the far post.
coaching.practice_design: Set-piece rehearsal against a zonal defensive shape mimicking the identified vulnerabilities: attacking side commits two runners from depth and two players holding offside positions to occupy/confuse the last defenders. All movement is triggered off a single, agreed cue (e.g. the taker's first step of the run-up). Rehearse the blocking player (matched physically against the opposition's weakest last defender) using a back-to-defender screen — no frontal contact, no arm use — to legally block the recovery run while remaining available for a second ball. Simultaneously rehearse the drag run that pulls the last defender infield, and the depth runner's timed, onside run to the far post. Finish with crosses/deliveries specifically inswinging to meet the far-post run.
success_cues: Attacking side identifies and exploits a genuine numerical advantage at the far post before the kick is taken.
Decoy/offside-holding attackers successfully occupy or confuse the last defenders without being the actual target.
All attacking movement triggers off the same cue, arriving synchronised rather than piecemeal.
The drag-run attacker pulls the last defender out of position, reducing far-post cover.

The blocking player is matched against a physically weaker last defender and executes a legal screen (back-to-defender, no arms, no frontal contact) that stops the recovery run without conceding a foul.
The runner from depth times his run to remain onside and arrives at the far post unmarked.
Delivery is inswinging and precisely meets the runner's arrival for a clean header on goal.

limitations: This article profiles a single detailed example (not multiple numbered clips like the corner articles), so 'clip 1' here refers to the sole PSG vs Inter Miami example described.

The article's separate 'Defensive solutions' section (Chelsea, Juventus, PSG's own defensive rotation, and Botafogo counter-strategies) is not included here as it describes different teams/situations, not this clip's defensive setup — flag if you want a separate case file for those.
